subject: chemistry-hl
about: Original practice questions written for the IB Chemistry 2025 guide (HL). Not IB past-paper questions or markschemes, and not a prediction of exam questions. Calculator-free practice: every item can be done without a calculator.

items.topicLabel: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
items.stem: Which process is sublimation?
items.note: Solid directly to gas. CO₂(g) → CO₂(s) is deposition.

items.topicLabel: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
items.stem: A sample is heated from 20 °C to 50 °C. What is the change in temperature in kelvin?
items.note: Kelvin and Celsius degrees are the same size, so the change is the same number.

items.topicLabel: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
items.stem: Which is a compound?
items.note: Fixed ratio of chemically bonded C and O; the others are mixtures.

items.topicLabel: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
items.stem: Which change of state is exothermic?
items.note: Condensation forms new attractions between particles, so energy is released. The other three need energy to overcome attractions.

items.topicLabel: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
items.stem: Which is a homogeneous mixture?
items.note: A solution has uniform composition throughout; the others have visibly separate phases.

items.topicLabel: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
items.stem: Which technique best separates ethanol (boiling point 78 °C) from water?
items.note: Two miscible liquids with different boiling points: fractional distillation.

items.topicLabel: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
items.stem: What is true of particles at absolute zero (0 K)?
choices: They have their minimum kinetic energy
They are all in the gas phase
They are at the freezing point of water
items.note: 0 K is the temperature at which particles have minimum kinetic energy; the kelvin scale starts there.

items.topicLabel: S1.1 Introduction to the particulate nature of matter
items.stem: While a pure liquid boils at constant pressure, its temperature stays constant. Why?
choices: Energy supplied overcomes attractions between particles
Covalent bonds inside the molecules break
The mass of each particle decreases
items.note: Energy goes into separating particles (overcoming intermolecular forces), not into raising average kinetic energy.

items.topicLabel: S1.2 The nuclear atom
items.stem: How many neutrons are in one atom of ⁵⁶Fe (Z = 26)?

items.topicLabel: S1.2 The nuclear atom
items.stem: Element X has two isotopes, mass 10 (20%) and mass 11 (80%). What is Ar?
items.note: 2.0 + 8.8 = 10.8; no calculator needed.

items.topicLabel: S1.2 The nuclear atom
items.stem: Which species has more electrons than protons?
items.note: Negative ion = electrons gained.

items.topicLabel: S1.3 Electron configurations
items.stem: Which electron configuration is correct for Cu (Z = 29)?
items.note: Copper is an exception: a full 3d sublevel and 4s¹.

items.topicLabel: S1.3 Electron configurations
items.stem: What is the maximum number of electrons in the n = 3 level?

items.topicLabel: S1.3 Electron configurations
items.stem: In the hydrogen spectrum, which transition emits visible light?
items.note: Drops to n = 2 are visible; n = 1 is UV; n = 1 → 2 is absorption.

items.topicLabel: S1.3 Electron configurations
items.stem: Successive IEs (kJ mol⁻¹): 496, 4562, 6912, 9543. Which group?
items.note: Big jump after the first electron: one valence electron.

items.topicLabel: S1.4 Counting particles by mass: the mole
items.stem: How many moles of ions are in 0.10 mol of Al₂(SO₄)₃?
items.note: Each formula unit gives 2 Al³⁺ + 3 SO₄²⁻ = 5 ions.

items.topicLabel: S1.4 Counting particles by mass: the mole
items.stem: What is the empirical formula of a compound with molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆?
items.note: Divide by 6.

items.topicLabel: S1.4 Counting particles by mass: the mole
items.stem: What volume of 0.50 mol dm⁻³ NaOH contains 0.010 mol?
items.note: V = n/c = 0.020 dm³.

items.topicLabel: S1.4 Counting particles by mass: the mole
items.stem: At the same T and p, 20 cm³ of CH₄ is burned: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O(l). What volume of O₂ reacts?
items.note: Gas volume ratio = mole ratio 1 : 2.

items.topicLabel: S1.5 Ideal gases
items.stem: Which conditions make a real gas behave most like an ideal gas?
items.note: Fast particles, far apart.

items.topicLabel: S1.5 Ideal gases
items.stem: A fixed mass of gas at constant volume is heated from 200 K to 400 K. The pressure:
items.note: P ∝ T (kelvin).

items.topicLabel: S1.5 Ideal gases
items.stem: What volume does 2.0 g of H₂ (M = 2.0 g mol⁻¹) occupy at STP?
items.note: 1.0 mol × 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹.
